title: Spinal ultrasound imaging and vascular dynamics in pain
author: Ding, Yu, et al.

steps.title: Prepare sterile artificial CSF
steps.instruction: Dissolve in sterile water the following salts to the indicated final concentrations (mM): 3 KCl, 125 NaCl, 26 NaHCO3, 1.25 NaH2PO4, 1 MgCl2, 10 D‑glucose, and 2 CaCl2; adjust pH to 7.3 and filter‑sterilize.

steps.title: Anesthetize rat with isoflurane
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia in male rats using isoflurane (R510‑22, RWD China) at 4–5 % concentration, then maintain at 1–2 % with O₂ inhalation throughout the surgery.

steps.title: Position rat in stereotaxic frame
steps.instruction: Secure the anesthetized rat in a stereotaxic frame to ensure precise surgical alignment.

steps.title: Perform laminectomy to expose spinal cord
steps.instruction: Make a midline incision directly above vertebrae L3–L5, dissect the skin parallel to the spine, and expose the spinous processes. Use a surgical drill to thin the sides of the spinous processes, grasp them with hemostatic forceps, and elevate to reveal the spinal cord. Trim any excess bone with fine scissors, taking care to avoid damage to blood vessels, achieving maximal exposure of the spinal cord tissue.

substeps.instruction: Trim excess bone with fine scissors.

steps.title: Insert subarachnoid catheter with ACSF
steps.instruction: Load a catheter tip with the prepared artificial CSF, insert the tip into the subarachnoid space of the exposed spinal cord area, and advance the top tube of the catheter through the sheath so that it is precisely positioned at the exposed L3‑L5 segment.

substeps.instruction: Fill catheter tip with sterile ACSF.
Insert tip into subarachnoid space at exposed cord.
Position top tube at L3‑L5 through sheath.

steps.title: Secure catheter and close incision
steps.instruction: Secure the catheter in place, suture the skin incision, and administer antibiotics to prevent post‑surgical infection.

steps.title: Post‑operative recovery and heating
steps.instruction: Place the rat on a 37 °C heating pad until it regains consciousness, then return it to its home cage for a one‑week recovery period.

substeps.instruction: Put rat on 37 °C heating pad until awake.

steps.title: Acclimate animals before experiments
steps.instruction: Allow the recovered rats to acclimate to the experimental environment prior to any testing.

steps.title: Analyze data with GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Use GraphPad Prism 7.0 to present all data as mean ± SEM. Apply logarithmic transformations, then test normality with the Shapiro‑Wilk test. For Gaussian‑distributed data, perform an unpaired two‑tailed t‑test; consider results significant when p < 0.05 and report the corresponding F‑values, degrees of freedom, and P‑values. Optimize all graphics with CorelDraw 2020.

substeps.instruction: Present data as mean ± SEM in Prism 7.0.
If normal, conduct unpaired two‑tailed t‑test.
Set significance threshold at p < 0.05; report F, df, and P.

description: Following one week of recovery from SNL surgery, male rats underwent a laminectomy procedure. Rats were anesthetized using isoflurane (R510-22, sourced from RWD China) at an induction concentration of 4-5 % and maintained at 1-2 % via inhalation of O2. They were then positioned in a stereotaxic frame for surgical precision. Guided by anatomical landmarks, an incision was made directly above the L3-L5 vertebrae. The skin was dissected parallel to the spine, revealing the spinous processes. A surgical drill was used to thin the sides of the spinous processes, which were then grasped with hemostatic forceps and elevated to expose the spinal cord. Any excess bone was trimmed using fine scissors, ensuring maximal exposure of the spinal cord tissue while carefully avoiding blood vessel damage (shown in Fig. 1A and B). Next, a subarachnoid catheterization was performed by inserting a catheter tip containing artificial cerebrospinal fluid into the exposed spinal cord area (shown in Fig. 1C). The top tube of the catheter inserted through the sheath is precisely positioned at the exposed area of the spinal L3-L5. This ensured precise drug delivery to the enlarged spinal cord segment, facilitating the investigation of drug effects on functional connectivity and blood flow in specific regions. The catheter was then secured, the incision sutured, and antibiotics administered to prevent post-surgical infection. Rats were placed on a 37 ˚C heating pad until they regained consciousness before being returned to their cages for a one-week recovery period. Before experimentation, animals were allowed to acclimate to the experimental environment.Fig. 1Spinal laminectomy and intrathecal catheterization. A. Window for L3-L5, B.
